chapter.title: Configuration
chapter.para: The hypervisor has no run-time configuration: its VMs are described once, in an XML file, and the hypervisor is built for that description. The same file serves both architectures.

section.para: The hypervisor shall take its configuration, that is its VMs (name, image, memory, CPUs, console port and GDB port) and the port of its own console, from a description that is fixed when it is built.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A fixed configuration is what makes the behaviour predictable.

section.para: The hypervisor shall not change its configuration while it runs.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A fixed configuration is what makes the behaviour predictable.

section.para: The configuration shall give the hypervisor one to eight VMs; each VM a name of 1 to 30 letters, digits and the characters underscore, dot and hyphen, which is unique when compared without regard to case; the image of a JetOS kernel built for the architecture of the hypervisor; a memory size that is a multiple of 2 MiB and at most 1 GiB; and a number of CPUs (one if not given).

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: These are the properties of a VM that the hypervisor needs.

section.para: The hypervisor shall be built only from a configuration that is consistent, the build rejecting an image that is for the other architecture or does not fit into the memory of its VM, a serial port used twice, more than 16 CPUs in all on x86_64 or 8 on arm64, and VMs and hypervisor that do not fit into 3 GiB of memory.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A configuration error is found when the hypervisor is built, not when it runs.

section.para: The configuration shall name serial ports as COM1 to COM4 on x86_64 (the four ISA ports), and as COM1 and COM2 (the PL011 ports) and COM3 to COM16 (16550 ports on the PCI bus) on arm64.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The ports are those of the computers that QEMU emulates.

section.para: The hypervisor shall be built as one image that holds its code, its configuration, the images of the VMs and their device trees (on arm64), and a CRC-32 of all of them.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The hypervisor and the VMs are loaded and checked as one.
